name: fleet-telemetry-ingestion
summary: Trucks send sensor readings to a central service that keeps the fleet manager informed.
goals: The system notifies people through an external channel.
Scheduled jobs process stored records in windows.
Devices publish over MQTT; the consumer persists before acknowledging.
Exports are dropped on an SFTP server.
Records move in and out as files.

rules: Every component logs one structured line per unit of work with the correlation id.
Prefer the boring option; a new piece of infrastructure needs a decision record.
Java 21 as stated in the constraints.
Stateless processes: configuration from the environment, no local files that a second instance would not see.
definition_of_done: Acceptance checks of the package pass.
No file outside the write scope changed.
Every public operation of the implemented interfaces exists with the declared inputs.

requirements.statement: Each truck publishes a batch of sensor readings (speed, fuel level, engine temperature, position) every 30 seconds over MQTT.
The service validates readings, drops duplicates, and stores them.
requirements.rationale: no catalogue pattern matched; owner chosen by the engine (see the notes)

requirements.statement: Fleet managers view the latest reading per truck and a 24-hour chart per sensor.
requirements.rationale: no catalogue pattern matched; owner chosen by the engine (see the notes)

requirements.statement: When engine temperature exceeds a threshold for more than 5 minutes the fleet manager is notified by SMS.
A nightly job aggregates readings into daily statistics per truck and exports them as CSV to an SFTP server.
5,000 trucks, 20,000 readings/s at peak; a reading is visible to managers within 10 s p95.
Readings are never lost once acknowledged to the truck; duplicates never appear in charts.

metric.name: lost or duplicate updates under concurrent writes to one record

requirements.statement: Raw readings are kept 90 days, daily statistics 5 years.
Java 21, PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB available, Kafka available. Team of 5. On-prem Kubernetes.
The MQTT broker already exists and is operated by another team.
Domain records are kept indefinitely; logs and audit history are retained for 1 year, after which a nightly job deletes them (assumed by the engine).
requirements.rationale: assumed by the engine; confirm or override

decisions.title: Caller authentication
decisions.context: Management operations must be attributable to a customer or operator.

options.name: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
cons: no delegation or expiry unless added

options.name: OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provider
Session tokens issued by the platform's own account service to game/mobile clients (device-bound, short-lived, refreshable)
No account: a reference number plus a knowledge factor (date of birth) resumes a saved application; every attempt rate-limited and logged
pros: no credentials to manage for occasional users
cons: a reference number can be shared; scope what it unlocks

options.name: Email one-time code / magic link (no account needed)

decisions.choice: API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a bearer token
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). API keys per customer, hashed at rest, sent as a: 1.29; OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provi: 1.00; Mutual TLS: 0.86; Session tokens issued by the platform's own acco: unavailable (needs game_client, not in the constraints); No account: a reference number plus a knowledge : unavailable (needs no_account_auth, not in the constraints); Email one-time code / magic link: unavailable (needs email_auth, not in the constraints)
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'OAuth2 / OIDC with the platform's identity provi' gives up: single sign-on, expiry and scopes. Not choosing 'Mutual TLS' gives up: strong, no secrets in headers.

decisions.title: Primary store
decisions.context: Domain records need durable, queryable storage.

options.name: MySQL / MariaDB (the stated database)
cons: weaker JSON and DDL ergonomics than PostgreSQL

options.name: Redis for the hot state (as stated) with a relational store for durable records
pros: the stated home of the hot data

options.name: Managed document store (DynamoDB/MongoDB, as stated)
cons: query patterns must be designed up front

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). PostgreSQL: 3.25; MySQL / MariaDB: unavailable (needs mysql, not in the constraints); Redis for the hot state: unavailable (needs redis_primary, not in the constraints); Managed document store: unavailable (needs document_db, not in the constraints); SQLite: unavailable (ruled out by containers); Files: unavailable (ruled out by containers); In-memory: unavailable (ruled out by containers, postgres, durable_required, on_prem). stated in the constraints

decisions.title: Process topology
decisions.context: The same code base serves requests and performs background work.

options.name: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
pros: independent scaling of ingress and outbound work

options.name: Single process with background threads
cons: request latency competes with outbound work

options.name: Separate services per concern (ingest, admin, delivery)
cons: three deployables for a team of three

decisions.choice: One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` processes scale independently
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). One image, role by flag: `api` and `worker` proc: 1.84; Single process with background threads: 1.45; Separate services per concern: 1.37
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Single process with background threads' gives up: one deployable. Not choosing 'Separate services per concern' gives up: clear ownership.

decisions.title: Work queue technology
decisions.context: Work items must survive a crash and be leased by several workers.

options.name: PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
pros: transactional with the domain data (persist + enqueue atomically)
cons: throughput bounded by the database (fine to ~10k items/s)

options.name: Redis Streams with consumer groups
pros: built-in consumer groups and pending lists
cons: separate from the transactional store: needs an outbox

options.name: Managed broker (SQS/RabbitMQ/Kafka)
cons: at-least-once semantics still need an outbox

decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). Managed broker: 2.94; PostgreSQL table with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP: unavailable (stated rate 20,000/s exceeds this option's ceiling of 10,000/s); Redis Streams with consumer groups: unavailable (needs redis, not in the constraints); In-memory queue: unavailable (stated rate 20,000/s exceeds this option's ceiling of 1,000/s). stated in the constraints

decisions.title: Time-series storage
decisions.context: High-rate readings must be written continuously and queried by time window.

options.name: TimescaleDB hypertables in PostgreSQL (time partitioning, compression, retention policies)
Plain PostgreSQL tables partitioned by day

decisions.choice: TimescaleDB hypertables in PostgreSQL (time partitioning, compression, retention policies)
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). TimescaleDB hypertables in PostgreSQL: 3.25; Plain PostgreSQL tables partitioned by day: 2.04; ClickHouse: unavailable (needs clickhouse, not in the constraints). stated in the constraints
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Plain PostgreSQL tables partitioned by day' gives up: no extension.

decisions.title: Concurrency control for conflicting writes
decisions.context: Two callers may change the same record at the same time and the result must be consistent.

options.name: Optimistic concurrency: version column checked on every update; conflict returns 409 and the caller retries
Row locks inside a short transaction (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)

decisions.choice: Optimistic concurrency: version column checked on every update; conflict returns 409 and the caller retries
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). Optimistic concurrency: version column checked o: 1.75; Row locks inside a short transaction: 1.71; Last write wins: 1.53
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Row locks inside a short transaction' gives up: simple mental model, no client retry. Not choosing 'Last write wins' gives up: nothing to implement.

decisions.title: Redundancy for the availability target
decisions.context: The availability target must be met through instance failures and deploys.

options.name: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
cons: needs stateless instances and a shared store

decisions.choice: Two or more interchangeable instances per role behind the ingress, health checks, rolling deploys
decisions.rationale: Scored against the active qualities; decided by durability (weight 1.0), performance (weight 0.9). Two or more interchangeable instances per role b: 1.51; Single instance with health-based restart: 1.29; Active-active across two regions: 1.22
decisions.consequences: Not choosing 'Single instance with health-based restart' gives up: simplest, cheapest. Not choosing 'Active-active across two regions' gives up: survives a regional outage.

risks.description: A widespread failure disables many targets and emails every owner at once.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit notifications per owner and batch them.

risks.description: A management operation reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate in one middleware for every management route; test every route unauthenticated.

risks.description: Entities evolve; migrations run against live data.
risks.mitigation: Versioned migrations applied before deploy; additive changes first, removals one release later.

risks.description: At-least-once delivery means a target can receive the same event twice (crash between call and ack).
risks.mitigation: Send a stable event id and attempt number in headers; document idempotent consumption; never retry on 2xx.

risks.description: Retried and dead-lettered items accumulate and slow the lease query.
risks.mitigation: Partial index on (partition, not_before) for live items; archive terminal items on a schedule.

risks.description: Payloads or uploads without size limits exhaust memory or disk.
risks.mitigation: Enforce size limits at the surface; reject early with a clear error.

risks.description: Parts of the requirements were not recognised by the catalogue and received a generic decomposition.
risks.mitigation: Review the components marked generic; refine responsibilities and interfaces before briefing.
Parameterised queries only; no string-built SQL. Check: static check for string-formatted SQL finds nothing

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Store: Backups and dumps contain everything.
risks.mitigation: Encrypt backups; restrict who can take them. Check: backup file is not readable without the key

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Work queue: A poison item is retried forever and blocks its partition.
risks.mitigation: Attempt cap and dead-letter; per-partition concurrency cap. Check: an always-failing item ends in the dead-letter after the cap

risks.description: [tampering] Work queue: Items are processed twice after a crash between call and ack.
risks.mitigation: Idempotent processing with the item id; ack only after the outcome is recorded. Check: kill the worker mid-call; the item is redelivered exactly once more

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Notifier: Notification storms and template injection.
risks.mitigation: Rate-limit per recipient; escape template context. Check: 1,000 failures produce one digest per owner

risks.description: [spoofing] Authentication: Credential stuffing or leaked keys.
risks.mitigation: Hash keys at rest; allow revocation; rate-limit failures. Check: revoked key is rejected within seconds; brute force is throttled

risks.description: [elevation] Authentication: A caller acts on another tenant's resources.
risks.mitigation: Every core operation takes the principal and checks ownership. Check: cross-tenant request returns 404/403 for every operation

risks.description: [spoofing] Public HTTP API: Requests without a verified caller identity reach domain operations.
risks.mitigation: Authenticate every route in one middleware; deny by default. Check: every route returns 401 without credentials

risks.description: [tampering] Public HTTP API: Malformed or oversized bodies reach the core.
risks.mitigation: Schema-validate and size-limit at the surface; reject before parsing fully. Check: fuzz the body; oversize returns 413

risks.description: [denial_of_service] Public HTTP API: A single caller saturates the service.
risks.mitigation: Per-caller rate limit and request timeouts. Check: burst from one key returns 429; others unaffected

risks.description: [information_disclosure] Public HTTP API: Stack traces or internal ids leak in error responses.
risks.mitigation: Map exceptions to fixed error shapes; log details server-side only. Check: no traceback text in any 4xx/5xx body
